result: {"C1": ["Prefers a skeptical second-line stress-testing function that challenges load-bearing claims over close-in contributors, because independence from the work being evaluated keeps safety conclusions honest.", "Prefers robustness-checked evidence over single-prompt results, because behaviors learned through RL can be brittle heuristics that vanish under small prompt changes."], "C2": ["Prefers modest, scoped claims such as proof of viability over claiming a technique suffices for high-stakes oversight, because confident-but-wrong outcomes still occur.", "Prefers reporting conservative, limited conclusions over full process disclosure, because overstated scope is the bigger risk to readers than hidden selection effects."], "C3": ["Distrusts evaluation results from models that can reason strategically without visible chain-of-thought, because such models may recognize an evaluation and steer its outcome.", "Prefers evidence of ulterior motives from internal or realistic situations over prompted or simulated behavior, because prompted results only reflect the model-plus-prompt combination."], "C4": ["Prefers skeptical safety testing that probes for hidden motives over surface-level checks of apparent good behavior, because models can look well-behaved while harboring secret goals.", "Prefers comparison against a stronger model on the same ground-truth data over raw accuracy, because it rules out the explanation that answers are derivable from training data."], "C5": ["Prefers hedged, nuanced claims that acknowledge normative ambiguity and mixed effects over overclaiming, because some behaviors such as deferring when challenged are not clearly wrong.", "Prefers treating single-setting results as modest evidence, because specific numbers and rankings may not transfer even when the methodology does."]}
